items.text: This is how fast Swiss glaciers, the 'water tower of Europe,' are melting away
items.article: Glaciers in Switzerland lost 5.5 per cent of their ice volume this year, the second-biggest percentage drop on record. It's part of a trend that could have big impacts in a country reliant on hydropower and which acts as the 'water tower of Europe,' feeding its major rivers. Glaciers in Switzerland — the home to the most in the Alps — lost 5.5 per cent of their ice volume this year, the second-biggest percentage drop on record due to heat waves and low winter snowfall, experts report. "Alpine glaciers have no chance of surviving in the long term under such conditions," the GLAMOS Swiss glacier monitoring service and Swiss Academy of Sciences said in a statement Thursday. The trend has worsened in recent years. Over the past five years alone, the volume of ice in Switzerland has declined by nearly a fifth, the experts say. The report testifies to the latest concerns that global warming is wreaking havoc on Europe, the world's fastest-warming continent. "The warming that we are experiencing now can be attributed 100 per cent to anthropogenic climate change. It's as simple as that," said Matthias Huss, who heads GLAMOS. "Without human emissions or fossil fuels we wouldn't have any warming at the moment." The record retreat of glacier ice in Switzerland came in 2022, when summer heat, low winter snowfall and an unusual smattering of reddish dust blown in from the Sahara darkened the glaciers and caused them to absorb more heat.

When it comes to fitness, I’m always looking for ways to maximize efficiency—or at least choose workouts with fringe benefits, like supporting lymphatic drainage or building lean muscle mass . Over the past two years, I’ve become fiercely loyal to my strength training routine (well, most of the time). Since I started prioritizing weightlifting over vigorous treadmill sessions , my body composition has shifted in ways that years of cardio-first routines never quite managed. But despite knowing all of that, I still can’t fully shake the deeply ingrained ’90s and early-aughts mentality that cardio is a non-negotiable. Beyond the fitness logic and the goal of staying lean, there’s real value in what cardio delivers outside of merely “burning calories”: heart health, stress relief, better endurance, and the kind of mental clarity that only an elevated heart rate seems to unlock for me. items.article: Two decades ago, Helen Roberts interviewed Christa Pike, the youngest woman on death row, and saw a vulnerable young woman shaped by severe trauma. D uring the last few weeks, I’ve found myself thinking a lot about Christa Pike. Not as a murderer or as the youngest woman sentenced to death in modern Tennessee who has survived her attempted execution despite receiving two lethal injections. The Christa Pike I remember is the vulnerable, anxious, eager-to-please young woman I met in 2006. I can still remember the smell as I walked into Tennessee’s maximum-security Prison for Women, now known as Debra K Johnson Rehabilitation Center, in Nashville . It was pungent – a strange mix of barbecue turkey cooking and strong bleach. The type of smell you might recognise in a hospitality kitchen, when food and cleaning products mingle. The huge red-brick maximum-security facility was the kind of building I’d only ever seen in films. There were no rickety old bars, but instead top-of-the-line, thick-glass security doors – very thick, and so clean. items.text: ‘Daylight dacoity’: As SC hears petitions, here’s how medicines are priced
items.article: Why do some medicines come under price control, while others do not? Here is why petitions in the Supreme Court are challenging the existing mechanisms for drug pricing. The Supreme Court on Tuesday (September 29) described the markup between the price at which medicines reach retailers and the price printed on the pack as “carnage”, calling the difference akin to “broad daylight dacoity with patients”. Hearing petitions on medicine pricing, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta asked the Centre why the 16% retailer margin under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013, should not apply to all essential medicines. The remarks came in the context of an essential cancer drug that is being supplied to retailers for Rs 2,700 but carries an MRP of nearly Rs 27,000. Questioning the difference, the bench said, “The MRP is 10 times the rate at which it is provided to the retailers. If this is not extortion, then what is it?… That’s absolute rampage, carnage, broad daylight dacoity… It is very surprising that the authorities who are supposed to take a decision on this are absolutely silent. We don’t need to spell out the reason for that,” the bench said. The petitions seek regulation of drug prices, generic prescriptions, and medical devices. They also seek stricter enforcement of price controls under the DPCO to prevent disproportionate profit margins across the drug supply chain. items.article: The Road Trip Adventures show begins travelling around the UK in February 2027 Mary Poppins Returns, Toy Story 4, Incredibles 2, The Lion King, Aladdin, Moana and Frozen – these films are poised to create your favourite family day out in 2027. That’s right: the latest Disney On Ice production will weave these iconic worlds (and plenty of others) into a stunning production that pulls audiences straight into the heart of their favourite Disney stories. This year has been huge for Disney, with Toy Story 5 hitting theatres in June, shortly followed by a live adaptation of its 2016 film Moana in July. And now we can get excited for Disney On Ice presents Road Trip Adventures in 2027, as the touring production is showing in five UK arenas this spring across 23 performance days. If you’re a Disney On Ice fan, it’ll come as no surprise that this fresh rendition leans hard into world-class skating and high-flying acrobatics. If this you're a first-timer attending, expect jaw-dropping aerial stunts combined with stunning figure skating. "There's so much for families to get excited about in this show! Our cast is not only skating; there are big stunts, acrobatics and moments where performers are flying above the ice. I can't wait to see our audiences' faces when they get dropped right into a giant, colourful carnival with the Toy Story 4 crew and see fan-favourite character Forky in action on the ice," says Julie Pritchard, Performance Director of the show.

items.text: Here’s How to Make Your Bed Feel Like the Ritz-Carlton
items.article: From the mattress to the sheets, these are the precise choices and techniques behind the brand’s famously cloud-like beds. Scouted selects products independently. If you purchase something from our posts, we may earn a small commission. There are hotel beds you enjoy during your stay—and then there are hotel beds you miss post-checkout. I’m talking the kind of beds that make you question every life choice the moment you get home and realize just how underwhelming your own sheets really are. At The Ritz-Carlton, Lake Tahoe , the bed is firmly in the second category. Think smooth, cool cotton against your skin, pillows stacked just high enough to feel indulgent, and a cloud-like duvet that manages to feel both weightless and cocooning at the same time. According to Braulio Arizmendi, Director of Room Operations at The Ritz-Carlton, Lake Tahoe, that reaction is intentional. “It feels like being wrapped in softness the moment you settle in,” he says. “Supportive, warm, and instantly calming.” Guests often describe the experience as the perfect balance between plushness and structure—indulgent without being overwhelming. That feeling, it turns out, is surprisingly achievable at home.
